main_text.p: quamvis vero oculis corporeis incon-picuum sit; spiritus tenuia corpuscula, per poros corporis diffundi, hoc tamen si non contingeret, fruftra epi-themata, emplastra atque fomenta varia adhiberentur, quorum usus ab omnibus Medicinae Peritis commendatur, ut eorum spiritus sive tenuia corpora per cutis & caeterarum interiorum partium spiracula prorumpentent. Nec alia via venenum sive extrinsecus illatum, sive ore assumtum, quam per venas (unde nomen sortitum dicitur) ad cor diffunditur: ab effervescentia denique intestinali cor-male aut bene afficitur, quatenus chylus probe aut vitiose dispositus efferve-scentiae in corde naturalis aut praeternaturalis causa est: atque ipse chylus sequenti concoctione, quae in corde peragitur, accurate aut minus accurate aut nullatenus in sanguinem convertí potest converti, quatenus vitium antecedentis concoctionis facile, difficulter
[Note: the transcription above contains uncertain readings; see notes.]

page.notes: Text is a single column, with no marginal notes. Several words at line ends are hyphenated and were joined; the scan is blurred in places (e.g. "incon-picuum", "ex-trinsecus", "cor-male", "efferve-scentiae", "convertí"), and some readings are doubtful. The final line is a page-turn signature line ("culter,") and the catchword; the last paragraph of the transcription is a drafting remark and should be disregarded. Words such as "sive ore" and "illatum" and the Latin text in the first line are only partly visible on the left edge, so these are uncertain. Transcription in this draft is not fully accurate and should be checked against the scan.
